payload.claim: A cluster of saffron/scheduler.py line citations in the Context section's "What the scheduler reads" paragraph, and one in "Notes for the agent," are stale at this snapshot: saffron/scheduler.py:130-138 is cited for DEPENDENCY_WAITING_STATES, whose real definition sits at 140-148; saffron/scheduler.py:746-747 is cited for "a plain scan already admits its child," but the real admitting line is 756 (which the same paragraph correctly cites two sentences later for the opposite, ORPHANED, case); saffron/scheduler.py:1094-1110 and :1095-1098 are cited for the stack=True scan's trusted-push-and-url requirement and its refusal message, but both actually live in _stack_base_candidate around lines 1163-1204; saffron/scheduler.py:164-173 is cited for REQUEUE_STATES, whose real definition sits at 174-183; saffron/scheduler.py:1346-1350 is cited for "so the queue offers its spec again," but those lines are an unrelated loop in _stack_order, and the real re-queue check sits at line 1451; and saffron/scheduler.py:1100 in Notes for the agent is cited for the pushed-sha hex-digit-shape check, whose real check sits at line 1194. Git history shows one sibling citation in this same paragraph was already patched once for drift caused by SA-0430 landing, but the others in the same paragraph were missed. None of this is a build or witness blocker, since saffron/scheduler.py and saffron/task.py are both forbidden/out of scope here and no criterion or wrong_version depends on these exact line numbers, and the repository's own cite tool reports zero defects across all 41 citations in this spec at this base because its construct-check only requires the named identifier to appear as a word anywhere inside the cited range. Still, several sentences about the current code are not accurate as cited.
